1.1.name: Contextual Down: crouch vs downward aim resolution

summary.decisions: (1) Hook-based wiring instead of moving capture into update.js: input.js keeps ownership of the freeze mechanics (angle storage, cos/sin feedback into aimX/aimY); update.js only supplies the contextual rule via setResolveAim(() => getHero().resolveAim(intent)) — no new module coupling, screens unaffected. (2) Capture uses dirAngle(dir) (the canonical DIR_ANGLES table) rather than atan2(sin/cos) reconstruction — the latter silently flips sign for dirs 1/2/7 (caught by test). (3) Resolver receives {down: s.crouch, lockMove, aimX: dirX, aimY: dirY} — the pre-freeze raw values — so the context rules see the true held state at press time.
summary.tradeoffs: Resolver wins over lastAim unconditionally when installed — even if the player had an explicit non-contextual aim in flight, engage-time resolution re-applies context rules per §5 'captures the resolved aim'. Screens never install a resolver so their raw-capture behavior is untouched. The frozen vector round-trips through aimFromInput exactly (verified all 8 dirs), so resolveAim's lockDir branch returns the captured direction.
summary.lessons_learned: (1) lastAim was already non-null on the engage frame (set by the previous poll's else-branch), so gating the resolver on 'lastAim === null' made it dead code — the capture must prefer the resolver whenever one is installed. (2) Math.atan2(Math.sin(d*PI/4), Math.cos(d*PI/4)) ≠ dirAngle(d) for dirs 1, 2, 7 (sign flip) — always use the canonical angle table when converting 8-way indices to angles. (3) Pipeline tests are order-sensitive to hero position/facing carried between cases; placeHero() settles the hero onto the floor each time which masks most drift but crouch-state assertions need the settle frames before locking.
summary.done: REVIEW FIX (lock-capture §5): Lock Direction now captures the RESOLVED aim at engage time, not the raw directional key. input.js gained setResolveAim(fn) — the gameplay layer (update.js) installs hero.resolveAim as the resolver; on the lock-engage frame (lockedAngle===null) the capture runs resolveAim({down: s.crouch, lockMove, aimX: dirX, aimY: dirY}) and freezes dirAngle(dir). Without a resolver installed (screens/pre-hero polls) the old raw-aim + facing fallback is preserved unchanged. A grounded crouched hero pressing I while holding Down now locks horizontal-toward-facing instead of straight-down. Also exported DIR_RIGHT/DIR_LEFT/DIR_DOWN from projectile.js (single shared table; hero.js local constants removed).

1.2.name: Air control: ramp from rest, preserve jump momentum

summary.decisions: Chose Option A (collision flag from resolve()) over the velocity heuristic or reordering jump logic: it is the only signal that distinguishes 'standing still about to move' from 'pinned against a wall', both of which have vx≈0. Flag lives on the entity (_blockedX) rather than being returned, so hero.update() can read it without the main loop needing new plumbing.
summary.lessons_learned: resolve() zeroes vx into walls every frame, so a blocked hero can never accumulate velocity — making vx alone an ambiguous blocked/rest signal. The distinguishing fact is whether a solid actually cancelled displacement this frame, which only the collision resolver knows. Tests that simulate blocking must set _blockedX=true (not just zero vx) to exercise the real code path.
summary.done: Replaced the velocity-based blocked heuristic in hero.js update() with a reliable collision flag. resolve() in collision.js now tracks whether any solid cancelled horizontal displacement this frame (blockedX) and stamps entity._blockedX; added wasBlockedX() helper. The horizontal branch now uses 'grounded && _blockedX' for the air-ramp decision instead of |vx| < epsilon, so a grounded hero at rest pressing a direction gets instant full run speed (§7) while a solid-pinned hero ramping out of a barrel still uses the §8 air ramp. Fixed the ground-snap test to start from natural rest (vx=0) and assert instant 250 on the first frame, and updated the barrel test to stamp _blockedX.
summary.tradeoffs: The block flag is stamped by resolve() at end-of-frame N and read during update() of frame N+1 (one-frame-late signal). This is correct for the barrel case because resolve() re-stamps it every frame while pinned, so the flag stays true across the whole pin duration including the jump-launch frame. Requires the main loop to call resolve(hero,...) — which it already does.
summary.failures: None for the required suites (airControl, jumpslide, contextualAim all exit 0). Note: heroHit.test.js and timers.test.js fail but are PRE-EXISTING baseline failures about the stale 'inv' timer label (separate task), verified via git stash.

1.3.name: Supermove: phase-aware jump cancellation + anim flag fix

summary.done: Fixed review findings on Task 1.3: (1) velocity ramp now uses a separate non-resetting _supermoveElapsed accumulator so vx is one continuous linear ramp SUPERMOVE_SPEED→SUPERMOVE_RESIDUAL across the whole dash — no discontinuity at the burst→decel handoff; phase split still governs gravity + jump-cancel only. (2) endSupermove restores intangibility as max(0, pre-grant - elapsed-since-trigger), so a short pre-dash grant that expired during the dash is correctly zeroed instead of resurrected from the shared timer's current value. (3) Removed the erroneous 'this.intangible = false' at the end of respawn() — the flag now stays true while the RESPAWN_IFRAMES timer is active (§27). (4) Added 3 tests to supermove.test.js: monotonic-decreasing vx across the full dash spanning the phase boundary, short pre-grant (0.3s) not restored after a 0.6s dash cancel, and respawn grants actual immunity (flag true, hit absorbed, clears after window).
summary.failures: heroHit.test.js retains its single known pre-existing 'inv' timer failure (takeHit sets recovery + invincible timers) — unchanged by this fix, no new failures.
summary.lessons_learned: A per-phase countdown timer must never be reused to derive whole-sequence progress when it resets between phases — keep a separate cumulative accumulator. When bumping a shared timer upward for a window, restoring the prior state requires subtracting real elapsed time from the captured pre-value, not clamping against the live timer.
summary.decisions: Velocity is a pure function of total elapsed time (_supermoveElapsed), decoupled from the per-phase supermoveTimer which resets at handoff. Intangibility restore computes remaining analytically (pre - elapsed) rather than reading the shared timer, since the timer was bumped to cover the dash.

1.4.name: Hit response: contextual knockback table + i-frame visual sync + test cleanup

summary.decisions: Chose to transfer the remaining intangible timer across hero swap (rather than clearing it) to preserve the player's earned i-frame window; also clear flag when timer is already spent so no orphaned flag survives Object.assign.
summary.lessons_learned: bck/object.test.js fails to load due to a pre-existing missing test/consts.js module — unrelated to these edits (it imports ../consts.js which does not exist); required suites (heroHit, timers, supermove) all pass.
summary.done: Applied 4 review fixes: (1) removed duplicate 'if (heroEnt.intangible) return;' guard in update.js contact handler; (2) deleted stale '(inv, rapid, rec, ...)' comment line in hero.js, keeping the corrected '(intangible, rapid, rec, ...)' version; (3) added 'if (e.intangible) continue;' guard to both explosion AoE loops (explodeBarrel in object.js and explodeJackolantern in jackolantern.js) so i-frames absorb explosion damage consistently with contact/projectile paths; (4) swapHero() now copies the remaining 'intangible' timer value to the new hero (and clears the flag if the timer already expired), preventing permanent immunity after a mid-i-frame switch.
summary.tradeoffs: Explosion intangibility guard placed in the pure AoE functions rather than at call sites — keeps the rule in one place per explosion type and matches how takeHit absorbs hits.

1.5.name: Crouch/slide cancellation hardening + anim-state sync audit

summary.done: Fixed the first-frame crouch grace bug: moved the wasCrouching capture to BEFORE the crouch entry/exit block in Hero.update() so it reflects the pre-transition state (previously captured after the entry block had already set this.crouching=true, making the grace condition dead code). Added a test in crouchCancel.test.js asserting that on the exact frame Down is first pressed while running, vx retains full run speed (250) and from the next frame slide decel removes exactly SLIDE_DECEL*dt (~8 px/s → 242).
summary.decisions: Captured wasCrouching at the top of the crouch section rather than using an enteredCrouchThisFrame flag; keeps a single source of truth for the pre-transition state and matches the existing comment intent.
summary.tradeoffs: None — minimal one-line move of the capture plus an explanatory comment.
summary.lessons_learned: The sliding flag is derived from crouching && |vx|>0.5, so it is legitimately true on the grace frame too — the grace governs control input, not the momentum-derived slide state. Don't assert sliding=false on the entry frame.
